exact_statement: For finite strictly positive lattice weights, the decreasing finite-box events E_n that a B_n-minimizing S_n-to-S_n path passes through 0 intersect exactly when a full-lattice bigeodesic passes through 0.
assumptions: E_n uses the induced finite B_n metric
proof_or_counterexample: First-exit truncation gives nesting; diagonal finite-prefix selection and comparison with each finite full-lattice competitor prove the limiting path is globally geodesic.

exact_statement: If E_n are decreasing F_n-measurable events and P(E_(n+1)|F_n)<=1_(E_n)(1-q_n) for F_n-measurable q_n in [0,1], then P(E_infinity and sum q_n=infinity)=0.
proof_or_counterexample: 1_(E_n)exp(sum_(j<n)q_j) is a nonnegative supermartingale since exp(q)(1-q)<=1; finite almost-sure limit contradicts divergence on E_infinity.
remaining_gap: Divergent predictable FPP hazards are unproved.

exact_statement: Under an iid nonatomic nonnegative law with mass arbitrarily near 0, an all-cheap perimeter ring at radius n+1 kills the box event E_(n+1) with positive conditional probability b_n=G([0,m/(8(n+1))))^(8(n+1)), but sum b_n is finite almost surely.
proof_or_counterexample: 8r independent ring edges; shorter arc cost <m/2 versus any origin path >=2m; G([0,m/(8r))) eventually <=1/2, so b_n<=2^(-8r).
remaining_gap: Specific ring hazards are summable; actual hazards may be larger.

exact_statement: Positive conditional kill probability at every stage need not imply extinction when those probabilities are summable.
assumptions: independent stage-n kill events with q_n=1/(n+1)^2
proof_or_counterexample: The survival product through N is ∏_(n=1)^N (1-1/(n+1)^2)=(N+2)/(2(N+1)), tending to 1/2.
remaining_gap: Abstract probability example only; not an iid FPP environment.

exact_statement: Unit edge weights on Z^2 admit the horizontal axis as a bigeodesic.
proof_or_counterexample: Each horizontal segment has cost equal to ℓ1 distance, a lower bound for every competitor.
remaining_gap: Does not apply to atomless iid weights.

exact_statement: For finite strictly positive weights, the decreasing events that some global S_R-to-S_R geodesic passes through 0 intersect exactly when a bigeodesic passes through 0.
proof_or_counterexample: Truncate a global witness at its first exits; finite candidate paths and diagonalization give a two-sided globally minimizing path. Incidental assertion that every pair has a geodesic for arbitrary positive weights needs deletion.
remaining_gap: Global event is not finite-box measurable for a conditional-hazard argument; no event-decay bound.
status: independently checked proof with prose fix

exact_statement: If q_R is the supremum of global origin-hit geodesic probabilities over unordered S_R pairs and (32R_j^2-4R_j)q_(R_j)->0 on an unbounded subsequence under a stationary law, then almost surely there is no bigeodesic.
proof_or_counterexample: There are 8R sphere vertices and binom(8R,2)=32R²-4R pairs; union bound, decreasing-event continuity, translation, countable union.
remaining_gap: The required pair bound is unproved.

exact_statement: Uniformly vanishing individual probabilities in a growing family need not make the union probability vanish, even for a nested union sequence.
proof_or_counterexample: Each piece has probability 1/M_R while their union is [0,1) for every R.
remaining_gap: Logical obstruction only; no FPP counterexample.

exact_statement: For iid nonnegative Z^2 weights with P(t_e=0)>0, almost surely a noninjective two-sided nearest-neighbor walk in row zero has every finite segment of minimum passage cost.
assumptions: repeated vertices allowed in the weakened definition
proof_or_counterexample: An iid horizontal zero edge exists almost surely since (1-p)^N→0; alternate forever between its endpoints. Every finite segment has cost zero, the minimum by nonnegativity.
remaining_gap: This is not an injective bigeodesic and does not address the nonatomic target.

exact_statement: Pointwise almost-sure exclusion for each fixed Busemann label rho cannot by itself exclude an environment-selected random label of a hypothetical bigeodesic.
assumptions: Ahlberg-Hoffman Theorem 2.6 is pointwise in fixed rho
the possible label set need not be countable
proof_or_counterexample: For U uniform on [0,1], P(U=rho)=0 for every fixed rho, but there exists rho=U with probability one; countable union reasoning does not apply to uncountably many labels.
independent_reviewer: pending external audit; w395 author checked the logical example
remaining_gap: A simultaneous random-label exclusion or a distinct whole-event proof; the 2026 preprint claims such a bridge but is not fully audited here.

exact_statement: Two positive finite full-lattice completions agreeing on all B_1 edges can disagree on the global S_1-through-origin geodesic event while the B_1-minimizer event remains identical.
assumptions: second completion S_2 perimeter and S_1-to-S_2 connectors weight 1/20, all other edges weight 1
proof_or_counterexample: In the second completion every S_1 pair has an outside bypass using <=10 cheap edges, cost <=1/2, while every path through 0 costs >=2. The first completion has opposite axial endpoints joined globally through 0. Inside B_1 weights are identical.
remaining_gap: Counterexample to substituting global E_R into an inside-edge filtration, not an iid FPP counterexample.

exact_statement: For a fixed gain M and deterministic finite neighborhood independent of partition refinement j, almost-sure distinct marked labels give convergence of retained-mark indicators and probabilities as bin mesh tends to zero; if neighborhood size grows with j this can fail.
assumptions: finite neighborhood fixed for each M
all marked center-neighbor labels distinct almost surely
nested partitions with mesh tending to zero
proof_or_counterexample: A finite maximum of pair-separation indices exists pathwise; bounded convergence gives probability convergence. With iid uniform labels, j equal bins, and 2j^2 neighbors, retention is (1-1/j)^(2j^2)->0 despite distinct labels.
remaining_gap: The preprint's distinct-label, comparison and mark-density premises were not established by this local limit check.

exact_statement: Conditional on the common Busemann-pair conclusion, union-metric preservation of both marked bigeodesics, and a strictly raised edge on one path outside the other's individual changed region, two distinct marks cannot have equal upper labels.
source: OpenAI, No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation (2026-09-24), Proposition 7.6, https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/No-bigeodesics-in-planar-first-passage-percolation-September-24-2026/main.pdf
proof_or_counterexample: Common Busemann pairs give B_+(k,u)+B_-(k,u)=0; calibration gives B_+(u,v)=t_e; detour excess L_N-D_N tends to zero. In the first individual metric its named edge saves g>0 and all other weights weakly decrease, contradicting geodesicity for large N.
remaining_gap: Corollary 6.2, Lemma 7.5, Proposition 7.4, and the rest of the preprint chain were not fully audited.
